# Willrun

> Willrun answers whether a specific portable power station or generator can run a specific appliance, using published running and starting watts, an 85% inverter allowance for stations, and 30 amp inlet math for home backup.

Willrun is a static site. Every station and appliance row cites a manufacturer or ENERGY STAR URL. Runtime is nameplate watt-hours times 0.85, divided by average draw. Verdicts are runs, runs with surge risk, won't run, or no run verdict when running watts were not published.

## Start here
- [Calculator](https://willitrunpower.com/): pick a station, add appliances, read the verdict.
- [Methodology](https://willitrunpower.com/methodology/): the 0.85 allowance, duty cycle, and how surge is treated.
- [Stations](https://willitrunpower.com/stations/): 24 models.
- [Appliances](https://willitrunpower.com/appliances/): 51 loads.
- [Affiliate disclosure](https://willitrunpower.com/disclosure/)

## Guides
- [Best power station for a refrigerator in a power outage](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/fridge/): ENERGY STAR median use by fridge type (top-freezer 363 kWh/yr, bottom-freezer 538, side-by-side 640, door-ice French door 715), a 1,200 W motor-start surge rule (Haier 805 W start-up; Champion 800–1,200 W), runtimes on 13 stations, capacity needed for 12 h to 3 days, and solar panel watts by state vs each station's solar input limit.
- [Best power station for a CPAP](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/cpap/): Buying guide by decision: humidifier vs heated tube (ResMed AirSense 11: 7 W off, 19 W humidifier, 55 W heated tube), DC converter vs AC (inverter idle draw about 15 W per BLUETTI, so AC humidifier-off nights are far lower than capacity ÷ watts), nights needed, UPS switchover times (DELTA 3 Plus and RIVER 3 Plus <10 ms; Jackery 1000 v2/2000 v2 and Anker C1000 <20 ms; RIVER 2 Pro <30 ms), ResMed Air11/Air10 DC converter current limits, auto-off timers, FAA 100 Wh flight limit, and maker medical-use caveats. Picks: DELTA 3 Plus, Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, BLUETTI AC180, RIVER 2 Pro, RIVER 3 Plus, Jackery Explorer 2000 v2, DELTA 2 Max.
- [Best power station for camping](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/camping/): For a carried campsite, the EcoFlow RIVER 2 (7.7 lb, 256 Wh) and Anker SOLIX C300 (288 Wh) cover a CPAP and lights; a Danby compact fridge pushes you toward the RIVER 2 Pro, DELTA 2, or AC180 if you can spare the weight.
- [Best power station for an RV](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/rv/): An 8,000 Btu/h BLACK+DECKER window unit draws about 533 W while cooling. Stations at or above 600 W continuous can hold that running load, and the DELTA Pro 3 and F3800 add 120/240 V outlets the smaller packs do not have. None of them publish a match for the compressor's startup watts.
- [Best power station for home backup](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/home-backup/): On stored energy alone, the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,096 Wh) outlasts the Anker SOLIX F3800 (3,840 Wh), while the F3800 has the higher continuous output at 6,000 W. A 1,500 W Lasko heater needs at least 1,500 W continuous or a documented resistive boost.
- [Best power station for a sump pump](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/sump-pump/): The Zoeller Model 53 at 115 V draws 1,115.5 W while running. Stations under that — including the RIVER 2 series, the AC70, and the Yeti 500X — will not hold it. Stations above it still carry a surge risk because Zoeller does not publish starting amps.

## CPAP and BiPAP
Watt figures come from ResMed's published therapy-device power table and the Philips DreamStation humidifier manual (80 W supply, used as a worst case). Medical pages carry a safety notice: estimates only, confirm approved power sources with the manufacturer and your supplier.
- [CPAP and BiPAP on battery power: every model and setting](https://willitrunpower.com/cpap/): A CPAP night costs anywhere from about 50 Wh to more than 500 Wh. The humidifier and heated tube decide the size of power station you need, not the machine.
- [Best power station for a CPAP](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/cpap/): Buying guide with picks by situation (bedside UPS, camping on DC, budget, multi-night heated humidity) and runtimes that include about 15 W of inverter idle draw on AC.
- [CPAP during a power outage: how long each setup lasts](https://willitrunpower.com/cpap-during-power-outage/): Turn the humidifier and heated tube off during an outage if your doctor agrees. On ResMed's figures that cuts nightly use from about 440 Wh to about 56 Wh.
- [CPAP camping: how to power a CPAP with no electricity](https://willitrunpower.com/cpap-camping/): For camping, turn humidity off and use the DC cord if your machine has one. An AirSense 11 then needs about 56 Wh a night, so a 256 Wh station covers about four nights.
- [How many watts does a CPAP use? Every ResMed setting](https://willitrunpower.com/how-many-watts-does-a-cpap-use/): ResMed measures its CPAPs at 6.3 to 7 W without a humidifier, 19 to 22 W with a humidifier, and 34 to 55 W with a heated tube.
- [BiPAP battery backup: ResMed AirCurve runtimes](https://willitrunpower.com/bipap-battery-backup/): A ResMed AirCurve BiPAP uses 8 to 9 W without a humidifier and up to 66 W with a humidifier and heated tube, close to a CPAP.
- [CPAP on DC vs AC: which lasts longer on a power station?](https://willitrunpower.com/cpap-dc-vs-ac-power-station/): Running a CPAP from a power station's 12 V port with the maker's DC cord skips the station's inverter, so it usually lasts longer than the AC estimates on this site.
- [Can a car battery run a CPAP? The real math](https://willitrunpower.com/can-a-car-battery-run-a-cpap/): A typical 12 V car battery can run a CPAP without humidity for a night, but deep discharges damage car batteries, and Philips warns against running its machines while the engine is running.
- [What size solar panel do you need for a CPAP?](https://willitrunpower.com/cpap-solar-panel-size/): To refill one CPAP night from the sun, divide the nightly watt-hours by your sun hours and allow for loss. Without humidity, a 50 W panel is plenty; with a heated tube, plan on about 150 W.
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirSense 11 with HumidAir 11 humidifier, no heated tube?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-airsense-11-humidifier/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirSense 10 AutoSet, no humidifier?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-airsense-10-no-humidifier/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirSense 10 AutoSet with HumidAir humidifier?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-airsense-10/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirSense 10 with HumidAir and ClimateLineAir heated tube?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-airsense-10-heated-tube/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirCurve 10 VAuto BiPAP, no humidifier?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-aircurve-10-vauto-no-humidifier/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirCurve 10 VAuto BiPAP with HumidAir humidifier?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-aircurve-10-vauto/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirCurve 10 VAuto BiPAP with HumidAir and heated tube?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-aircurve-10-vauto-heated-tube/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirCurve 11 VAuto BiPAP, no humidifier?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-aircurve-11-vauto-no-humidifier/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirCurve 11 VAuto BiPAP with HumidAir humidifier?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-aircurve-11-vauto/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirCurve 11 VAuto BiPAP with HumidAir and heated tube?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-aircurve-11-vauto-heated-tube/)
- [Will a power station run Philips DreamStation, worst case at the 80 W power supply rating?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/philips-dreamstation-max-rated/)

## Outages
- [24-hour outage](https://willitrunpower.com/outage/24-hour/): EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max, EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3, BLUETTI AC200L, Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus, Jackery Explorer 2000 v2, Anker SOLIX F2000 (PowerHouse 767), Anker SOLIX F3800 have enough nameplate watt-hours, after the 85% allowance, for this 24-hour mix (1,608 Wh of load).
- [3-day outage](https://willitrunpower.com/outage/3-day/): No base unit in this set stores enough for this mix. The load is 4,823 Wh, which needs about 5,675 Wh of nameplate capacity after the 85% allowance, and nothing here is that large without an extra battery.
